# Prologue

Captain Marcus Gavin sat staring dumbfounded at the screen on the wall, the large display was an older model, one that had seen its share of mission launches and training exercises, despite all of this it still showed the growing horror in high definition for the entire control room to see. The few personnel left in the room made up about 1% of its capacity. Those left to man the last mission mankind would ever send into the darkness of space Marcus thought.

The first age of man ended much as it had begun with silence.

At the close of the 22nd century, Earth stood empty, bereft of humans, void of their monuments. The beasts once again ruled the planet. The instrument of man's demise, the alien weapon, found beneath the ice of Earth, now stood as the last temple to technology on the small blue world.

Though Earth stood empty of man, the universe did not. Seeing the end coming, humanity, in a last desperate act to save itself, created the ARC.

With the advanced knowledge gleaned from the alien weapon, humankind now could safely enter a frozen state of slumber and awaken centuries later.

The last remnants of humanity, twenty thousand souls in all, slept away the ages, aboard the massive ship as it floated out near mars until it was safe to step foot upon the globe once again.

The grand ARC, man's best hope for a future, eventually returned to the little blue planet, the last evidence of man's mastery over the machine, stood sentry over the small blue world.

The ship's artificial intelligence watched and waited, the machine standing vigil, analyzing, and scanning the world man once called home. Only once the world was again deemed safe were the PODS release back to the now-feral world, the slumbering inheritors of man's destiny.

Frozen in the small pods, they would rocket back to the planet, allowing man once again to take their rightful place upon the Earth.

However, some did not return. Either by accident or some purpose not understood by man or machine, they floated above the planet, locked in orbit, locked in sleep, randomly falling to the world as the age's past.

Those who paid attention to such things called them fallen, here is the story of one lost soul, robbed of his world and returned to an earth which has regressed to a time long before his own.
